claims.claim: A population is the group about which a claim is made; a sample is the subset observed. Random sampling can reduce systematic selection distortion when the sampling frame is appropriate. Convenience samples can differ from the target group. Larger samples reduce some random variation but do not repair systematic exclusion or nonresponse. A survey's question wording, collection method and target population all matter. Sampling and causal experimental assignment are different design choices.
